prospects.thesis: Intel's +33.5% one-month rip reflects a fundamental turnaround narrative taking hold as foundry customer wins and 18A process node ramp gain credibility, with bullish options and institutional flow confirming smart money conviction. As a domestic pure-play foundry alternative to TSMC, Intel is a direct beneficiary of CHIPS Act tailwinds and reshoring policy momentum. Entry now captures the transition from "show-me" to "execution" phase before mainstream re-rating.

AMD's MI350/MI400 accelerator roadmap is finally translating into hyperscaler wins, and the +29.2% monthly move reflects growing acceptance as the credible #2 AI GPU vendor behind NVDA. With options, institutional, and momentum all aligned bullish, AMD offers leveraged exposure to AI capex without NVDA's crowding risk. Near-term catalyst is Q4 data center guidance and MI400 customer disclosures.

KLA dominates process control and metrology equipment, an indispensable pick-and-shovel play on every advanced node ramp at TSMC, Samsung, and Intel. As leading-edge complexity increases (gate-all-around, backside power delivery), KLA's inspection tools become more essential per wafer, driving structural margin expansion. Bullish smart money signals and a +11.5% monthly gain suggest institutions are positioning ahead of a 2027 WFE capex up-cycle.

ARM's architecture licensing model provides royalty exposure to every major AI inference chip, custom hyperscaler silicon (AWS Graviton, Google Axion), and the mobile/edge AI wave. The +19.4% monthly move and bullish positioning are compelling, but the 59.8x P/S is stretched and demands patience for a better entry. Near-term catalyst is v9 royalty rate expansion flowing through FY reports.

CACI provides mission-critical IT, SIGINT, and electronic warfare solutions to DoD and intelligence community customers, positioning it squarely in the software-defined defense modernization thesis. The recent -1.4% pullback offers a contrarian entry against a backdrop of record defense budgets and bullish options flow signaling accumulation despite bearish institutional tape. Adds portfolio diversification away from the semiconductor concentration and provides low-beta exposure to the defense theme.

Financials going bullish alongside that is the tell that this isn't a recession trade — it's a "soft landing plus deregulation" trade, likely tied to expectations around looser bank capital rules and continued M&A thaw under the current administration's lighter-touch approach to antitrust.
